correctness.rationale: Exact conditional uniformity of the graph outside a specified k-vertex tree component gives the covariance formula. A direct cross-product expansion equals (n-k-1)(k(n-3)+2)/2+k r>0, implying the monotone ratio and at most one sign crossing. The e^{-2alpha} hypergeometric-product limit gives the macroscopic threshold, and strict concavity gives its uniqueness. The bundled verifier passed 41472 exact checks including exhaustive G(n,m) enumeration for n<=6. Experiments are not used as proof of unbounded claims.

value.rationale: The sharp one-crossing classification is complete across every admissible n, k, and fixed edge count m and works uniformly over tree shapes. The transition in the sign of the initial covariance at k/n near 0.796812 ties a natural macroscopic component-size parameter to otherwise competing isolation statistics. Such large tree components are rare, a concrete limitation, but the exact boundary and model-dependent dependence interpretation are substantive rather than arbitrary tabulations.
